evals.prompt: Use an-dr-convention-layout. Lay out a new Rust repository for "mixer": a desktop app plus two libraries, core and audio. Show the folder tree with crate names.
evals.context: Empty repository. The app needs build.rs and run-time icons; the project uses an xtask for packaging.

evals.prompt: Use an-dr-convention-layout. I generated an STM32F4 project with CubeMX for CMake. Where does my application code go, and how do I test it without the board?
evals.context: The repository holds blinky.ioc, Core/, Drivers/, cmake/stm32cubemx/, CMakeLists.txt, and CMakePresets.json as CubeMX wrote them.
expected_behavior: Keeps the generated folders as CubeMX writes them and puts the application in components/ outside them, touching generated files only inside USER CODE blocks with calls into the components.
Splits hardware access into hal-interface, hal-stm32, and hal-host components so the app component builds and is tested on the development machine from tests/.

evals.prompt: Use an-dr-convention-layout. My PlatformIO firmware has to run on an Arduino Uno and an ESP32, and I want to unit-test the control logic on my PC. How should the project be laid out?
evals.context: Existing project: platformio.ini with one env, src/main.cpp, and a copy of a registry library pasted into src/.
expected_behavior: Uses one platformio.ini with an environment per board and a native environment, never a second project copy.
Moves the control logic into a framework-free library in lib/<name>/ tested from test/, and declares the registry library in lib_deps instead of copying it.
